title: Critics Slam Batman vs. Superman Movie
main_content:
“Batman vs. Superman: Dawn of Justice” is a movie a lot of people are excited about.

Since the Batman movie series started in 1989, movies with Batman have sold almost $2 billion of tickets in the U.S.

The same site says since 1978, the six Superman movies have sold over $800 million in tickets.

So, putting the two characters together, should result in a big movie.

But what happens if critics do not like it?

We will find out on Thursday night, when the film comes out in the U.S.

Some early showings have produced disappointing reviews.

Some critics say the two-and-a-half-hour film is too long.

One critic from the magazine Us Weekly calls it “151 minutes of gloom and doom.”

Another critic, Michael Phillips from the Chicago Tribune, says, “humankind deserves a better blockbuster.”  The headline of his article is “Yawn of Justice.”

But not every reviewer hates the film.

So far it looks like lots of fans ignored the reviews and purchased tickets.

questions.question: Why did people think “Batman vs. Superman: Dawn of Justice” would be a big movie?
options: Because both characters have a long history in film with significant ticket sales.
Because it is directed by a well-known filmmaker.
Because it was marketed heavily on social media.
Because it features multiple superheroes teaming up for the first time.
questions.answer: Because both characters have a long history in film with significant ticket sales.
